findings.title: Renamed function breaks existing callers
findings.body: The function was renamed from `readSensor` to `sampleSensor`, but `src/alerts.ts` still imports and calls `readSensor` on line 2. This will cause a runtime `ReferenceError` for any caller that hasn’t been updated. Either revert the rename or update all imports to match the new name.

findings.title: Magic number in temperature conversion
findings.body: The divisor `10` is a magic number. It’s unclear why the raw sensor value is divided by 10 to get Celsius, and the constant isn’t named or documented. Extract it to a named constant (e.g., `RAW_TO_CELSIUS_FACTOR`) with a comment explaining the conversion.
findings.suggestion:
const RAW_TO_CELSIUS_FACTOR = 10;
  return { id, celsius: sensor.raw() / RAW_TO_CELSIUS_FACTOR };

summary.problem: Renaming `readSensor` to `sampleSensor` breaks existing callers and a magic number reduces readability.
summary.done_well: The function signature and return type remain consistent with the existing interface.
